verdicts.reason: alloc_init_cont_pmd, init_pmd, init_pte and set_permissions support table reuse, zeroing and EFI perms, but in-place safe permission changes are allowed and __create_pgd_mapping_locked is ABSENT.
asids_init/update_limit and is_write_abort match, but flush_dcache_folio only clears PG_dcache_clean for lazy flushing, and do_tag_recovery disables MTE checking rather than classifying faults.
cpu_context stores x19-x28, fp, sp, and pc, and thread_struct embeds cpu_context along with tp_value/tp2_value (TLS), fault_address, fault_code, and mte_ctrl.
init_kernel_el, __primary_switch, map_kernel, set_ttbr0_for_lpa2, and remap_idmap_for_lpa2 directly confirm EL setup, MMU table switching, kernel segment mapping, and LPA2 ID-map remapping.

overall: Findings 3 and 4 are fully supported by the cited arm64 headers and boot code; Finding 1 is partial due to an absent symbol path and permitted in-place permission updates, and Finding 2 overstates lazy PG_dcache_clean clearing and MTE tag recovery.
